abstract.text:
Abstract. A new notion of equilibrium, which we call strong equilibrium, is introduced for time-inconsistent stopping problems in continuous time. Compared to the existing notions introduced
in (Huang & Nguyen-Huu, 2018) and (Christensen & Lindensjö, 2018), which in this paper are
called mild equilibrium and weak equilibrium respectively, a strong equilibrium captures the idea
of subgame perfect Nash equilibrium more accurately. When the state process is a continuoustime Markov chain and the discount function is log sub-additive, we show that an optimal mild
equilibrium is always a strong equilibrium. Moreover, we provide a new iteration method that can
directly construct an optimal mild equilibrium and thus also prove its existence.

evidence.quote: The second notion of equilibrium, which we call weak equilibrium in this paper, is proposed in (Christensen & Lindensjö, 2018) and further investigated in (Christensen & Lindensjö, 2020).

predecessors.why: The paper treats their weak equilibrium as an alternative continuous-time stopping-equilibrium notion.

evidence.quote: In time-inconsistent optimal stopping problems, we introduce the following concept of strong equilibrium, which is inspired by (Huang & Zhou, n.d.).

predecessors.why: The paper says its strong-equilibrium stopping notion is inspired by their equilibrium-control work.

evidence.quote: To sum up, the economic interpretation of being “equilibrium” for mild and weak ones is inadequate.

targets.why: The paper argues mild equilibrium can degenerate when the time of return is zero and therefore lacks a full economic deviation interpretation.

evidence.quote: However, similar to that for time-inconsistent control (see e.g., (Björk et al., 2017, Remark 3.5) and (Huang & Zhou, n.d.)), the first-order criterion does not correspond to the equilibrium concept perfectly: when the limit in (1.6) equals zero, it is possible that for all ε > 0, x < Ex[δ(τSε)XτSε], in which case there is an incentive to deviate.

targets.why: The paper contends that the weak-equilibrium first-order condition can miss profitable deviations when the limit is zero.

evidence.quote: A new notion of equilibrium, which we call strong equilibrium, is introduced for time-inconsistent stopping problems in continuous time.

thesis.text: For time-inconsistent stopping in continuous time, a new strong equilibrium notion better captures subgame perfect Nash equilibrium, and under log-subadditive discounting an optimal mild equilibrium is strong and can be constructed by a direct iteration.

corrections.reason: The DOI recorded for this paper (10.1137/18M1216432) is not the DOI of this work: it is the DOI of a *different* paper by the same authors, the discrete-time mean-standard-deviation stopping paper, as the paper's own reference list shows. The paper itself carries no own DOI; only an arXiv identifier. The DOI should be removed or corrected.
